name: Ibn al-Haytham’s optics of vision
description: Ibn al-Haytham combined geometrical and observational reasoning in an account of vision by light entering the eye.

date.label: Approximately 1011–1050
date.basis: Two retrospective accounts give different estimated composition periods; the interval envelopes their estimates and is not a surviving manuscript date.

events.statement: Ibn al-Haytham composed the Book of Optics in the early eleventh century, within a broad interval encompassing differing scholarly estimates.

evidence.supports: Sabra dates the treatise to the second quarter of the eleventh century.
Describes vision through incoming light and mathematical and empirical optics.
A separate retrospective dates writing to 1011–1021.
Describes vision through incoming light and mathematical and empirical optics.

earliest_record.rationale: Broad estimated composition interval from differing secondary accounts, not the date of a surviving manuscript.

caveats: Sabra places composition in the second quarter of the century, while another retrospective gives 1011–1021. The broad interval reflects disagreement rather than a claimed period of continuous writing; the account drew on earlier optical and anatomical traditions.

research.note: Independent reading checked the source-supported event and chronology. Grain and other unreviewed facets remain provisional.
